purpose: Session lifecycle of the engine's global state: what a load puts back, what survives an unload and why that is harmless. T14 extends it with the causal save/restore policy of every component.
method: A clean process has every engine global at its static initial value and a second load in the same process does not. The step probe (tests/step/step_probe.cpp) loads the same image again in one process and compares it with a clean one: per-unit state digest (P6_RELOAD, P6_DIGEST_PARTS) and the writable data segment right after the reset head (P6_DATA_DUMP, diffed against nm). Heap growth is measured with Apple's leaks tool on p6_cycles_probe. Every entry that changes the engine has a test that failed before the change.

status_values.reset: put back to its clean-process value at load or reset; the test named in evidence compares a reload with a clean process
status_values.rebuilt: derived again from other state before anything reads it; a reload's video and machine digests match a clean process from unit 1
status_values.noncausal: a pointer, a counter that is only written, or a feature the A500 profile never reaches
status_values.open: differs from a clean process and is not understood yet; limitation of the profile until closed

entries.at_load: bridge/lifecycle.cpp clears regs before init_m68k; m68k_reset2 sets only pc, sp and sr, so D0-D7/A0-A6 would carry the previous session
bridge/lifecycle.cpp sets vpos to 0; custom_reset never resets it, so the first unit's length depended on how long the previous session ran (905 colour clocks in the measured case)
patch 0068 puts the head on track 0 in DISK_init; a p6_reset keeps it where it was, like a real drive
patch 0069 clears them in inputdevice_reset; POTGOR read $5500 instead of $0000 in the first frame of a reload
patch 0070 clears them in clear_events; event2idx decides where MISC_handler starts its round, so the order of two events due at the same instant
patch 0071 clears it in CIA_reset; it is compared with regs.ipl_evt when an interrupt is recognised and the cycle counter restarts at every reset

p6_input_reset_keys (patch 0066) runs at every p6_reset and, from bridge/lifecycle.cpp, at every load: a reset chord held when a session ended made the first key event of the next load reset the machine

matchdevices allocates a name and a configuration name per device on every load; copy_prefs memcpy'd the pointers away. Patch 0072 gives each preference set its own strings and bridge/config.cpp frees both sets when the session ends: 2.3 KiB per cycle, 68 KB in 30 cycles, now 0 leaks
see docs/adr/0007-audio-delivery.md
see reports/tasks/T12c.md: the registered blobs, the drive contents, the event queue and the sequence number are forgotten at unload

bridge/lifecycle.cpp sets the engine's cycle counter to 0 before p6_rtc_init and installs counter_restarts in p6_counter_restart_hook (patch 0073), which the reset head calls just before the counter starts over for EVERY kind of reset (p6_reset, the Ctrl-Amiga-Amiga chord, the reset warning): it adds the part of the unit that ran before the restart to the caller's ticks and rebases the clock, which keeps time through a reset. Before this, any guest that read the clock after a p6_reset or a reload faulted the image (p6_run_frame failed: 11), a Kickstart reads it at boot, and a first version that rebased only for p6_reset left the keyboard chord faulting
release_engine undoes exactly the stages the load reached: clock, video presentation, blob store, media identity
not cleared: per-line and per-frame drawing state that the drawing code overwrites before it reads it
not cleared: nothing reads them outside debugging (vsync_cycles is never read)
not cleared: the token of the next stream only has to be unique, p6_blob_clear closes every stream
allocated again at every load; their values are addresses of this process
not cleared: the Ricoh clock, the joystick port configuration, text pasting and the mouse time base are not reached by the A500 profile or do not show in a reload

cia_cycle_accurate is worked out once per frame (end of CIA_vsync_prehandler), so a process that has not finished a frame has it false and runs its first frame with CIA interrupts that do not wait for the E clock. A reload kept the last session's true: the keyboard interrupts of unit 1 came 8 to 11 colour clocks later and the last one stacked another PC, one byte of the stack ($F80118 instead of $F80116), for input_all and input_rotate. Patch 0074 puts it back from bridge/lifecycle.cpp at every load; a p6_reset keeps it, as a reset in a running process does

A session that moved the mouse left the quadrature counters behind (mouse_x/y, mouse_frame_x/y), the pending movement (mouse_axis, mouse_delta), the frame counters getvelocity() divides by and the host edge detector; the next load started JOY0DAT from them ($0A10 instead of $0101 for input_all after a script that moves the mouse). The idle reload of T13b could not show it. Patch 0075 puts them back from bridge/lifecycle.cpp at every load; a reset inside a session keeps them, as the hardware does. The bytes the data-segment diff still shows after a dirty session (mouseupdate's mxd/myd, stored_jports, the key ring, staterecords, can_inject's counter) only feed the host edge detector, a configuration log or code that is idle without text injection

session.audio_frames_total ('stereo frames Paula produced since load') and session.handed_over were not put back by p6_load: a reload added its frames to those of the previous session and started with the last unit's flag. Neither changes what the machine does (the count is only read by the state probe, the flag is cleared at the start of every unit), which is why no reload test saw them; the state probe did. p6_load now sets both to their clean-process value

savestate.purpose: Every causal component of the A500 profile with its owner, what upstream saves of it, what upstream omits, what must never be serialized, how it is rebuilt, and which test proves its restore. Written from a read of the materialized upstream tree (audit of T14a); the save/restore functions are a catalogue of what upstream considers state, not code that is compiled in.

audited.profile: A500: 68000 cycle-exact, OCS/ECS chipset, Chip and Slow RAM, Kickstart or micro-ROM, DF0/DF1 read-only ADF, joystick, mouse, keyboard, emulated RTC
audited.evidence_lines: path:line in evidence are lines of the materialized tree of that series; lines move with every patch, so the tests check that the files exist and the lines fit in them, not what is on them

policy_values.serialize: the upstream serializer covers it and nothing causal is left out
policy_values.serialize_extended: an upstream serializer exists but leaves causal variables out; the named extension adds them
policy_values.extension: upstream has no usable serializer for this causal state; T15 writes one
policy_values.rebuild: derived from other state after a restore; acceptable only with a test that shows equal futures
policy_values.noncausal: does not influence the emulated machine
policy_values.out_of_profile: never reached by the A500 profile; a state that carries it is rejected

findings.finding: SAVESTATE is not defined by the profile (ports/portable/sysconfig.h) and the whole container of savestate.cpp (ASF header, save_chunk/restore_chunk, save_state_internal, restore_state) is under #ifndef P6_PORTABLE, so there is no upstream format and no upstream save_*/restore_* for the CPU, the chipset, the CIAs, the floppies or the blitter in the binary. Only save_audio/restore_audio, save_input/restore_input and the drawing.cpp BPLX and Denise-sprite serializers are compiled, and nothing calls them.
findings.consequence: T15 writes its own container (docs/adr/0009-state-format.md). The upstream save_*/restore_* functions are read as the catalogue of what each module considers state, not reused as they are: enabling SAVESTATE drags in guarded runtime branches and the functions are lossy (next findings).

findings.finding: Where the upstream functions exist they do not describe a machine that continues bit for bit: they are made for a restore that reruns part of the reset and tolerates small timing differences. Examples: CIA-B TOD loses tod_event_state/tod_offset and restore_cia assigns the timer B latch to the TOD latch (cia.cpp restore, c->tol = w); save_cia mutates the live CIA; CHIP drops VPOSR/VHPOSR and forces vpos; the Denise input ring rga_denise, the Denise register copies, dmal_shifter and the copper WAIT/SKIP states are not saved; CHPD keeps event2 slots 1..15 and 11 handler ids and runs any other handler at once; CHSL restores slot pointers it cannot map as NULL; audio loses dat2, mixvol, the DAC samples, the anti-alias accumulators, the filter rc state and the resampler phase; DISK loses dsklen2, linecounter, the integer part of disk_hpos and the delayed disk change; CPU saves neither halted nor spcflags and restore_cpu_finish refills IR/IRC from memory.
findings.consequence: Each such component is 'serialize_extended' or 'extension' in `components` with the omitted variables named; T15 has to serialize them itself and prove each with a test that changes the field before the save.

findings.finding: SPCFLAG_UNIT_END is set once per rendered field at vpos == vsync_startline + 1 (custom.cpp), so a snapshot taken at a unit boundary is at vpos 4, a little after hpos 1, with almost a whole line of unprocessed Denise input in rga_denise and with the keyboard poll phase (hsync_counter & 15), prev_strobe and the copper in the middle of their sequences.
findings.consequence: The state has to be captured as it is at that boundary, with the rga_denise ring and the beam latches; draining the ring or rerunning part of the reset to get a clean line would change the future.

findings.finding: Some causal state is function-local or file-local and unreachable from the bridge: m68k_go_unit's `suspended` and `hardboot` statics (after a fresh load they send the next APPLY/RUN through the whole reset head: memory_clear plus a random start-up delay that eats emulated cycles), event2_newevent_xx's `next` allocation pointer (tie-break order of simultaneous events), cycles_to_add_remain, the keyboard poll phase, the pending key ring of keybuf.cpp (neither p6_reset nor the keyboard-only KEYB chunk cover it) and the live PRNG state.
findings.consequence: A restore must not run the reset head, and T15 needs patches that add accessors or serializers next to each of these; a state_load that only writes the chunks would continue differently.

findings.finding: A session in which the mouse moved leaves mouse_x/mouse_y, mouse_frame_x/y, mouse_axis and the mouse edge and delta statics of inputdevice.cpp behind: a reload of input_all after a script that moves the mouse reads JOY0DAT $0A10 where a clean process reads $0101. The idle reload of T13b did not show it, because nothing had moved in the first session.
findings.consequence: Same class as T13b/T13c and found by this audit: fixed in T13d (patch 0075, p6_input_session_begin, and a dirty-session reload test that fails without it).

findings.finding: The reset head reseeds the PRNG from currprefs.seed at every hard reset (uaerandomizeseed under P6_PORTABLE, newcpu.cpp), so a p6_reset draws the same start-up delay as the power-on; docs/02-contracts.md and p6.h said that the random seed keeps advancing across a reset.
findings.consequence: The documents are corrected in T14a. The live PRNG state (xorshiftstate/randseed) is still causal between resets: floppy jitter, the start-up delay and the chip colour power-up draw from it, and no chunk stores it.

findings.finding: There is no codegen hash anywhere; P6_UPSTREAM_COMMIT, P6_PATCH_COUNT, P6_PATCH_SERIES_SHA256 and P6_PROFILE are definitions of the p6_headless target only, so p6_bridge cannot put them in a state header; the compiler and its floating-point flags are in no identity.
findings.consequence: T15 adds a build-identity translation unit to p6_bridge (series hash, upstream commit, codegen hash, profile id, state format version) and decides, with a cross-compiler determinism test, whether the compiler belongs in it.

findings.finding: A Waterbox snapshot captures the dirty pages of the sandbox, including every static above and the rga_denise ring, and needs none of the extensions; it does not capture state that lives in the C# wrapper.
findings.consequence: The two formats and their hashes are separate by design (docs/adr/0009-state-format.md): a native state is never loaded into Waterbox nor the reverse, and their digests use different domains and are not comparable.

findings.finding: Comparing the digests of a reload with those of a clean process (T14b) showed two bridge fields that a load did not put back (session.audio_frames_total, a write-only diagnostic count that kept adding to the previous session's frames, and session.handed_over) and one bookkeeping counter that is not state (the video pass_counter). The audio registers, the chipset latches, the input pot model and the dead scheduler events differ at unit 0 too, before the power-on reset head has run; from unit 1 every subsystem matches for six fixtures.
findings.consequence: bridge/lifecycle.cpp resets the two bridge fields at load (T14b); unit 0 is not compared; a reload equals a clean process from the first unit on for every subsystem a probe sees. The state the probes cannot see is the audit's pending list.

components.component: D0-D7, A0-A6 and the two stack pointers (A7 = USP or ISP)
components.reset: m68k_reset2 (loads only A7 from vector 0 and PC from vector 4); bridge memset(&regs) + init_m68k at p6_load
components.saved_fields: 15 x u32 regs.regs[0..14] (D0-D7, A0-A6); USP = A7 when S=0 else regs.usp; ISP = A7 when S=1 else regs.isp. The inactive stack pointer is saved in its own slot, the active one through A7; MSP exists only for 68020+ and is not written for model 68000.
components.rebuild: m68k_reset_sr() selects A7 = isp (S=1) or usp (S=0) from the restored SR. Reset gap to keep in mind: m68k_reset2 does NOT clear D0-D7/A0-A6, usp or isp (the bridge only clears regs at load), so a p6_reset after running is not a function of the saved chunk alone.

proof.what: save at a boundary, continue in the same process and in a new one: the same digests, picture and audio

components.component: SR, CCR (regflags), T1/T0/S/M, interrupt mask
components.reset: m68k_reset2: S=1, intmask=7, T1=T0=M=0, X/N/Z/V/C cleared
components.saved_fields: regs.sr (u16) after MakeSR(): T1, T0, S, M, IPL mask, X, N, Z, V, C. MakeFromSR_x forces T0=M=0 on a 68000, so only T1, S, mask and the five flags are live.
components.pointers: regflags (struct flag_struct) is the live CCR: two u64 on x86_64, two u32 elsewhere, with host-layout bit positions (Z at bit 6, N at 7, V at 11, C/X at 0). Never serialize it raw; serialize the five SR bits.
components.rebuild: m68k_reset_sr() rebuilds regflags, t1, t0, s, m, intmask and A7 from regs.sr. It does NOT rebuild SPCFLAG_TRACE (MakeFromSR_x sets it only when T1/T0 change): see cpu-spcflags.

components.component: pc_p / pc_oldp host pointers and per-instruction scratch (opcode, instruction_pc, trace_pc, instruction_pc_user_exception)
components.reset: m68k_setpc_normal in m68k_reset2; memset(&regs) at load
components.saved_fields: None: upstream stores the PC only as a 68k address.
components.omitted: opcode, instruction_pc, instruction_pc_user_exception and trace_pc are not saved. On the 68000 CE core they are rewritten before any read (r->opcode = r->ir and r->instruction_pc = m68k_getpc() every iteration); trace_pc is read only by Exception_build_stack_frame_common (020+/MMU path), instruction_pc_user_exception only by debugmem. With m68k_pc_indirect = 1 (cycle-exact, set by build_cpufunctbl) m68k_setpc_normal zeroes both; Exception_ce000 still calls the direct m68k_setpc, so they may hold a host pointer, but pc_p - pc_oldp is always 0 and m68k_getpc() equals regs.pc.

components.component: 68000 prefetch queue: IR, IRC (and the write-only IRD / read_buffer / write_buffer / db)
components.owner: build/upstream/newcpu.cpp (regs.ir, regs.irc, regs.ird, regs.read_buffer, regs.write_buffer, regs.db)
components.reset: m68k_reset2: irc = 0xffff then fill_prefetch() (reads IR/IRC through the CE bus path, consuming emulated cycles)
components.saved_fields: regs.irc and regs.ir (u16 each) in the base block; ird, read_buffer, write_buffer (u16 each) in the model<=68010 block (flag 0x2000000).
components.omitted: regs.db and regs.last_prefetch are not saved. db is write-only in the profile (its only readers are inside #if 0 in custom.cpp and in the CPUEMU_21 block of cpu_prefetch.h); last_prefetch is never referenced. ird/read_buffer/write_buffer are saved but no 68000 CE handler (op_*_14_ff) reads them: read_buffer/write_buffer are read only on 68010 branches (Exception_ce000 else-branch, exception3_read_prefetch_only, newcpu_common.cpp).
components.rebuild: Restore IR and IRC verbatim. restore_cpu_finish() ends with fill_prefetch_quick(), which overwrites ir, ird and irc with get_word(PC) and get_word(PC+2); IRC/IR can legitimately differ from memory (prefetch taken before a write by the CPU or a DMA), so the native restore must skip that call.

components.component: Interrupt pipeline: ipl[2], ipl_pin(_p), ipl_evt(_pre/_mode), ipl_pin_change_evt(_p), lastipl
components.reset: m68k_reset2 clears only ipl[0], ipl[1], ipl_pin (and lastipl); ipl_pin_p, ipl_evt, ipl_evt_pre, ipl_evt_pre_mode and both ipl_pin_change_evt keep stale absolute times of the previous counter epoch
components.saved_fields: model<=68010 block: ipl[0], ipl[1], ipl_pin, ipl_pin_p as s8; ipl_evt, ipl_evt_pre, ipl_pin_change_evt, ipl_pin_change_evt_p as u64 absolute cycle counts.
components.omitted: ipl_evt_pre_mode (int 0/1): update_ipl() picks ipl_fetch_next vs ipl_fetch_now from it when c == ipl_evt_pre + cpuipldelay2, so it decides the IPL sampled by an interrupt that changes mid memory cycle. lastipl is not saved but is used only when m68k_interrupt_delay is false (not the profile). The saved u64 times are absolute: valid only if currcycle is restored to the same epoch.
components.pointers: m68k_accurate_ipl, m68k_interrupt_delay, cpuipldelay2/4 are derived flags (see cpu-dispatch-tables-and-mode-flags), not state. The delayed-IPL path (doint_delayed event2) is used only with cs_ipldelay, which is false in the A500 preset.

components.component: Halted CPU (double fault, invalid start address, opcode fetch from non-existing memory)
components.owner: build/upstream/newcpu.cpp (regs.halted; gui_data.cpu_halted is only a mirror)
components.reset: cpu_halt_clear() at the start of m68k_reset2
components.saved_fields: Nothing. The flags word of the CPU chunk carries STOP, not HALT, in spite of the doc comment 'bit 0=CPU was HALTed'.
components.omitted: regs.halted (int, CPU_HALT_* id 1..13). It survives a unit boundary: m68k_go_unit() re-enters the wait loop from it (waiting = regs.halted || CPUINRESET) and cpu_halt() also forces intmask=7 in SR. A restore that drops it resumes execution from the halted PC. crash_auto_reset is pinned to 0, so the machine stays halted until a reset.
components.pointers: gui_data.cpu_halted is a host-side mirror set by cpu_halt() and cleared by cpu_halt_clear(); do not serialize. haltloop() has a function-static prevvpos that only gates a no-op cpu_sleep_millis().
components.rebuild: Extension: one int. On restore set regs.halted and SPCFLAG_CHECK (m68k_go_unit does the latter itself for a halted CPU).

components.component: Special flags word (regs.spcflags): TRACE, DOTRACE, CPUINRESET, CHECK, INT/DOINT, BLTNASTY, UNIT_END
components.reset: m68k_reset2 (regs.spcflags = 0); custom_reset (unset_special(~(BRK|MODE_CHANGE|CHECK)))
components.saved_fields: Nothing: neither save_cpu nor any other chunk stores spcflags; restore relies on m68k_reset2 zeroing it.
components.omitted: Causal bits at a unit boundary: SPCFLAG_DOTRACE (trace exception pending for the next instruction, set by do_trace/activate_trace in the pass that ended the unit), SPCFLAG_TRACE (must equal T1|T0 but MakeFromSR_x sets it only on a change, m68k_reset_sr does not), SPCFLAG_CPUINRESET (CPU held in reset by the keyboard reset chord, cpu_inreset; m68k_go_unit resumes into the wait loop). SPCFLAG_CHECK is derivable: haltloop consumes it, and m68k_go_unit sets it again from regs.halted when it resumes. Inert in the profile: INT/DOINT (m68k_interrupt_delay and m68k_accurate_ipl are true, so doint() never sets them), CPU_SLOW (only with JIT or m68k_speed<0), BLTNASTY (loop guarded by !blitter_cycle_exact), UAEINT/TRAP/EXEC/ACTION_REPLAY (no producers). UNIT_END (value 1) is cleared by m68k_go_unit before it returns.
components.pointers: volatile uae_atomic word written with atomic_or/atomic_and (ports/portable/atomic.cpp); the atomicity is a host detail, serialize the plain value.
components.rebuild: Extension: save the DOTRACE and CPUINRESET bits verbatim; on restore also set TRACE if T1|T0 and CHECK if regs.halted (m68k_go_unit does the latter itself). Everything else is recomputed by the first do_specialties pass.

components.component: Exception-in-flight statics: last_*_for_exception_3, exception_in_exception, hardware_bus_error, regs.exception, TRY/CATCH frames
components.reset: None (never reset); written just before each use
components.saved_fields: None.
components.omitted: last_op/addr/fault/writeaccess/size/fc/di/notinstruction_for_exception_3 and last_sr_for_exception3 are assigned by exception2_setup/exception3f/exception2_fetch_common immediately before every Exception(2|3) and never read across instructions. exception_in_exception is set to -1/1 while a frame is written and back to 0 at the vector read on every 68000 path (the -1 early exits need regs.vbr&1 or a nested group-0 fault while writing the frame), so it is 0 at each boundary; assert it. hardware_bus_error is written only by hardware_exception2(), which has no compiled caller (memory.cpp calls sit under #ifndef P6_PORTABLE; default_xlate halts instead). regs.exception is 0 outside ExceptionX.

components.component: Stack-resident state of the instruction loop (locals of m68k_run_1_ce / do_specialties)
components.reset: Nothing to reset: m68k_run() enters m68k_run_1_ce() afresh on every unit
components.saved_fields: None. The unit ends inside do_specialties() (live read of SPCFLAG_UNIT_END), m68k_run_1_ce returns with exit=true, m68k_go_unit() returns M68K_UNIT_DONE. No C++ frame survives.
components.omitted: Locals r, first, exit of m68k_run_1_ce, the local spcflags snapshot of do_specialties, and handler locals are dead at the boundary. The two statements after do_specialties (ipl[0]=ipl[1]; ipl[1]=0) have already run, so the saved ipl[] are the post-shift values. A resumed run starts at 'r->opcode = r->ir' with first=true, which only calls set_cpu_tracer(false) (cpu_tracer stays 0).
components.pointers: TRY/CATCH (C++ try/catch in this build, mmu_common.h) holds no state while no exception is thrown.

components.component: m68k_go_unit function statics and reset-request globals (hardboot, suspended, in_m68k_go, quit_program, cpu_hardreset/keyboardreset, cpu_prefs_changed_flag)
components.reset: M68K_UNIT_BEGIN sets hardboot=1, suspended=false, in_m68k_go=1; M68K_UNIT_LEAVE clears them
components.saved_fields: None: upstream's m68k_go reconstructs this on the stack and has no resume concept.
components.omitted: suspended (bool) and hardboot (int) are function-local statics of m68k_go_unit, unreachable from outside. After a load they are suspended=false, hardboot=1, so the first APPLY/RUN runs the whole reset head: build_cpufunctbl, custom_reset, m68k_reset2, memory_clear and a random start-up delay that eats emulated cycles. A native restore must enter the suspended path (suspended=true, hardboot=0) or it destroys the restored machine. in_m68k_go (=1 while loaded) and quit_program (must be 0 at a boundary; uae_reset sets it negative) are plain globals. cpu_hardreset, cpu_keyboardreset and the loop-local 'restored' (always 0: its only writers sit in the compiled-out SAVESTATE blocks) are transient inside the head; cpu_prefs_changed_flag stays 0 because currprefs == changed_prefs.
components.pointers: suspended/hardboot are function statics: a patch must export a setter or make them file statics. Nothing here is a host pointer.
components.rebuild: Extension: patch newcpu.cpp so the restore path can set suspended=true, hardboot=0 (and assert quit_program==0 and SPCFLAG_MODE_CHANGE clear); in_m68k_go comes from p6_load.

components.component: Identity inputs for config_hash, media_manifest_hash and the core build id (what the bridge can hash today)
components.saved_fields: config_hash (from bridge/config.cpp): p6_config fields as given: abi_version (1), struct_size (72), machine (A500 = 1), video_standard (PAL 1 / NTSC 2: sets ntscmode, the chipset clock, FLOPPY_WRITE_LEN and the clock rate), audio_rate_hz (44100 | 48000 -> sound_freq), flags (0), random_seed (u64; folded to 32 bits into currprefs.seed, config.cpp:56-59), rtc_epoch_seconds (i64, years 1..9999), reserved[4] (0). The rest of the preset is a function of the build and the profile: profile_id 'deterministic-a500' (P6_PROFILE, manifests/source-manifest.json 'profile') and the field list of config/profiles/a500-ocs.json (upstream/pin/override values), verified at load by check_preset. Do NOT hash: render flags, input packets, host paths, callbacks, unit_index, mounted-disk state. | media_manifest_hash (from bridge/media.cpp and session.h): firmware_sha256 (SHA-256 of the firmware buffer exactly as passed to p6_load, not of the decoded ROM), media_count, and media_content_id[0..count-1] in p6_load order (32 bytes each; order is semantic because events and drive_media use indexes); media type (ADF only) and size 901120 are implied. The 'media-<hex>' blob ids and 'p6-firmware.rom' are derived. | core build id (from the identity macros printed by the headless adapter and the codegen manifest): P6_UPSTREAM_COMMIT (857f48fcb09399d4d95527e29a2fdeaedb41f827, from manifests/source-manifest.json 'commit'), P6_PATCH_COUNT (74) and P6_PATCH_SERIES_SHA256 (SHA-256 of patches/winuae/series.json, which embeds every patch sha256 and before/after file hashes: this is the patchset_hash), P6_PROFILE, P6_ABI_VERSION (1), plus the excluded-feature list (source-manifest selection.features_off) and the state format_version of the ADR.
components.omitted: Gaps found: (1) no codegen_hash exists: manifests/codegen.json lists generators, flags and environment but no output hashes and CMake defines no macro; the generated sources (cpuemu_13.cpp, cpustbl.cpp, cpudefs.cpp, blit*.cpp) need a file(SHA256) fold or a hash of codegen.json plus the upstream/patch hashes. (2) P6_UPSTREAM_COMMIT, P6_PATCH_COUNT, P6_PATCH_SERIES_SHA256 and P6_PROFILE are compile definitions of the p6_headless target only (CMakeLists.txt:101-105); p6_bridge and the libretro core do not receive them (libretro has its own P6_LIBRETRO_VERSION, cmake/Libretro.cmake:8), so the serializer needs them on p6_bridge or a generated header. (3) Compiler id/version, target ISA and the float flags (-fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off, CMakeLists.txt:42) change Paula's float results and are not in any identity yet: a native state is 'exact build', so they belong in the build id. (4) random_seed folding: two 64-bit seeds with the same fold give the same machine, hashing the 64-bit value is stricter than needed but safe. (5) cs_eclockphase travels inside CIAx chunks and must be checked against the config, not applied.

CD32 and CDTV are excluded features of the profile (sysconfig.h refuses to compile them)

FILESYS is an excluded feature: no host file system is ever exposed
no network device in the deterministic profile
arcade and laserdisc boards, HRTMon, the debugger memory watch points, the configuration text and the log are not part of the profile or of the machine state

probes.digest: SHA-256 over 'p6/probe/v1/<subsystem>', a zero byte and the canonical fields: fixed-width little-endian integers in a fixed order, no padding, no addresses

status_values.implemented: every field of the component is among those the probe hashes (`covers` names them and the test finds them in the source)
status_values.partial: the subsystem's probe covers the part of the component that can be reached from outside the engine; `why` says what waits for an accessor
status_values.pending: no probe can see this state until T15 adds an accessor

wrapper.purpose: State of the PUAE6 core (integration/bizhawk/core/Puae6/Puae6Core.cs) that the sandbox snapshot does not contain, or that the wrapper must not leave behind (T21b). Every instance field of the class is listed, with what it is and why it is or is not in a state; tests/waterbox-state/test_wrapper_inventory.py compares this list with the fields the compiled class has (by reflection), so a field that is added without being classified fails the test.

policy_values.saved: A field of WrapperState: written in the state, validated before the sandbox is touched and put back by a load. It has a causal effect on a later unit, or is a counter that BizHawk shows or a movie depends on, or is the output that the state's own frame has to show.
policy_values.construction: Fixed when the core is created and never changes afterwards; what a state is valid for is checked against it by the envelope (guest, heaps, config, firmware, media), so a state never needs to carry it.
policy_values.output: A buffer that every unit rewrites completely before BizHawk reads it; stale after a load until the next unit, which is what BizHawk expects of a core (the picture shown after a load is the last one drawn).
policy_values.cleared: Reset by a load: it belongs to the timeline that was left.
policy_values.lifecycle: Not a property of the emulated machine: object lifetime and error state.

_guest.what: the loaded guest: host, BizInvoke bindings and the identity that was verified

_syncSettings.what: the sync settings; the config hash of the envelope covers every one of them

_domains.what: BizHawk's wrappers of the guest's memory areas; function hooks, they hold no address of the machine's memory

_media.what: the disks the core was given; the media hash of the envelope covers their contents and order

_identity.what: what a state is valid for

_videoBuffer.what: the last picture, converted to ARGB

_soundFrames.what: how many frames of _soundBuffer BizHawk has not taken yet

_faulted.what: a state load failed after the sandbox was touched: no unit and no save until a state loads whole

Frame.what: units run since ResetCounters or since the movie's origin

IsLagFrame.what: the last unit read no input register

CycleCount.what: master ticks of the last unit

_aspectNum.what: pixel aspect of the last picture

_aspectDen.what: pixel aspect of the last picture

DriveLightOn.what: drive light of the last unit

_mouseKnown.what: the pointer position is known, so the first unit does not jump

_mouseReferenceX.what: where the machine was last told the pointer was: the next delta is measured from here

_capsHeld.what: the Caps Lock button was down in the previous unit: a held button does not toggle again

_driveDisk.what: the disk in each drive, for the on-screen messages only (not causal: the machine's own drive state is in the snapshot)

_currentDrive.what: the drive that Eject and Insert act on

_currentSlot.what: the disk that Insert puts in

_mediaSequence.what: the last sequence number given to the machine, which only grows

ControllerDefinition.what: the buttons and axes; they depend on the sync settings and on whether there are disks

InputCallbacks.what: BizHawk's input callback list; the machine has no callback per input read, so nothing ever calls it
